newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria abolishes visas for EU, EFTA visitors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria abolishes visas for EU, EFTA visitors.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet agreed on Thursday to abolish visa requirements for nationals of the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Area (EFTA) visiting for up to 30 days.
Foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev told reporters Bulgaria hoped the EU would now waive visa requirements for Bulgarians.
"Bulgaria sees the introduction of a 30 day visa free stay for the EU and EFTA countries as a step to ease the access of Bulgarians to the EU and EFTA in return," he said.
Visas are available on arrival at Sofia airport but cost $91. The decision comes into force once it is published in the Official Gazette.

Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said his ministry would at the same time tighten border controls for nationals of countries outside Europe because negligence in this area was one reason why the European Union put Bulgaria on the Schengen list of countries with restricted access to member states.
EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek is due to visit Bulgaria on March 17.
